title: Plum's Perimeter Puzzle
markdown:
OH! OH! Get ready, because this is the best part! You are going to LOVE this story. It’s about Oren, who makes the most beautiful kites you ever did see—kites shaped like sparkly dragons, giggling clouds, and even wobbly bumblebees that buzzed with joy in the sky! And he had a best friend named Plum. Plum wasn’t a kite, oh no! Plum was a rabbit. A super-duper fluffy, hop-tastic rabbit with ears that could hear a dandelion puff from a mile away and a nose that wiggled like a tiny, happy dancer when she was pleased.

Now, Plum loved to zoom. She’d zoom around her little rabbit run like a furry blur. She’d zoom past the juiciest carrots, her little legs a whirlwind. She’d zoom under the little shady bush, her white tail flashing like a tiny flag. But her fence… oh dear, her fence was getting a bit wobbly. It looked like it had danced a jig in a hurricane and completely forgotten how to stand up straight. One moment it was leaning left, the next it was wobbling right, making Plum feel a little dizzy.

“Plum, my little zoomer,” Oren said one sunny morning, scratching his head so hard his hair stood up like a startled dandelion. “This fence needs fixing. You need a super-safe, extra-zoomable space where you can do your best zooming without any wobbly surprises. I’m going to build you a new one, the best rabbit run ever!” He grabbed a big piece of paper, the kind that rustled like autumn leaves, and a sparkly blue pencil that left trails of shimmering light. He drew a perfect, neat square for Plum’s run. “There!” he declared. “Now, I need some bright, colorful edging to go alllll the way around the bottom. It will stop any sneaky weeds from popping through and give you a nice, clear border for your super-fast zoom-tracks. But…” Oren’s brow furrowed. “But… how much edging do I actually need? This drawing is just a drawing! It doesn’t tell me the *real* length.” He looked at the drawing, then at Plum, who was watching him with wide, curious eyes, then back at the drawing. His eyebrows did a little dance of confusion.

Plum twitched her nose, a sure sign she was thinking very hard. She nudged Oren’s hand with her soft, velvety head. She understood about needing more zoom-space for exciting adventures and speedy dashes. But the “how much” part? That was a bit like trying to catch a sunbeam in a teacup—slippery and confusing! They needed help from someone who knew about all sorts of clever things.

“Wait, wait, I know!” Oren suddenly exclaimed, his eyes lighting up like a kite catching the sun. “Gran Maple! She knows *everything* about measuring and making things look absolutely beautiful in her garden. She’s probably measured more things than there are petals on a thousand roses!” And off they went, Oren carrying his important sketch and Plum doing a little excited hop-skip-hop, her ears flapping with anticipation.

When they arrived at Gran Maple’s cottage, the air smelled like warm earth and sweet blossoms. Gran Maple herself was humming a cheerful tune, a melody as gentle as a summer breeze. She was carefully placing little, shiny blue tiles along the very edge of her prize-winning petunias. The tiles were the color of a clear sky, and they made a neat, straight line, like little soldiers standing guard around the vibrant pink and purple flowers.

“Gran Maple!” Oren called out, a little out of breath. “We have a bit of a kerfuffle!”

Gran Maple smiled, her eyes crinkling at the corners like ancient, wise maps. “Hello, Oren! And hello, little Plum! What’s all the excitement?” Her voice was warm, like a cozy blanket.

Oren eagerly showed her his drawing of Plum’s new rabbit run. “I need to put some colorful edging around Plum’s new rabbit run, Gran Maple,” he explained. “It’s a square, see? Like this.” He pointed to the neat lines on his paper. “But I don’t know how much edging I need. I tried to measure the drawing, but it’s just a drawing, and it feels too small to tell me the real size!”

Gran Maple chuckled, a sound like dry leaves rustling happily on a path. She picked up one of her bright blue tiles. “You see these tiles, Oren?” she said, holding it out. “I lay them down, one after another, right next to each other, to make a line. This line follows the very edge of my special flower bed. Each tile is exactly the same size, so when I count them, I know how long my flower bed is along *this* edge.” She gently ran her finger along the row of tiles. “This tells me how much space my flowers have to stretch their roots. If I wanted to put a little fence *all the way around* my flower bed, I would do the very same thing for every single side, counting the tiles for each one.”

Oren’s eyes widened. He looked at his drawing of the square, then at Gran Maple’s tiled path, which was now a neat, colorful border. He looked at Plum, who was giving a little bunny-wiggle, as if she understood perfectly. Suddenly, it clicked! His brain went *PING!* like a tiny bell ringing with a brilliant idea.

“That’s it!” Oren shouted, doing a little happy jump that almost made Plum hop right into a shiny watering can. (Don’t worry, she didn’t! I’m just exaggerating for fun. Mostly.) “Plum, we can do that at home!”

They thanked Gran Maple, their hearts full of new ideas, and hurried back. Oren rummaged through his workshop and found a pile of smooth, grey stones, each about the size of his thumb. They were perfect! Plum, eager to help, nudged them with her nose, which was surprisingly good for nudging stones into straight lines. She was determined to create the best zoom-space for herself.

Oren placed one stone. “That’s one bit of the edge,” he said. Then he placed another stone right next to it. *Clink.* “That’s two bits.” He kept going, *Clink, clink, clink,* placing each stone carefully, so they touched end-to-end, all the way along one side of the square he had marked out for Plum’s run. He counted aloud, his voice filled with concentration, “One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight stones!”

Then he moved to the next side of the square. *Clink, clink, clink.* Plum nudged a few into place with her whiskers twitching with intense focus. “Nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen stones!” Oren announced, a grin spreading across his face.

He did it for the third side. *Clink, clink, clink.* “Seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty, twenty-one, twenty-two, twenty-three, twenty-four stones!” he counted, his voice rising with excitement.

And finally, the fourth side. *Clink, clink, clink.* The stones clicked together like puzzle pieces. “Twenty-five, twenty-six, twenty-seven, twenty-eight stones!” he finished with a flourish.

Oren looked at all the stones laid out in a perfect square. He carefully counted them all up again, just to be sure. Eight and sixteen and eight and eight made… twenty-eight! “Twenty-eight stones!” he cheered, throwing his hands up in the air. “That’s how many stones it takes to go all the way around Plum’s new run! This is exactly how much edging I need!”

He realized that the total distance around the outside of something, like Plum’s square run, has a special name. It’s called the **perimeter**. The perimeter is just the total length of all the sides added up, like a path that goes all the way around! Knowing the perimeter meant he knew exactly how much colorful ribbon to buy.

With his new knowledge of perimeter, Oren went to the craft shop and bought a long, bright red ribbon, a zig-zaggy yellow one, a stripey blue one, and a grassy green one. He made sure they added up to twenty-eight stone-lengths, just like his measurement.

Soon, Plum had a beautiful, super-sturdy new rabbit run! It was the best run ever. She zoomed and zipped and whizzed and whirred in her extra-safe space, leaving perfect, tiny zoom-tracks all around the colorful, cheerful edging. She could run and hop and explore to her heart’s content, feeling completely secure.

“Thank you, Oren!” Plum squeaked, nudging his hand with her wet nose, her way of giving him the biggest bunny hug.

Oren smiled, feeling as happy and light as a kite on a windy day. “You’re welcome, Plum! And guess what? Now I know all about perimeter! It’s like a secret code for measuring things! I wonder what else I can measure with it. Maybe my kite-tails? Or the path to the berry bush in the woods? Or even the edge of my bed! The world is full of exciting things to measure!” And Plum, with a happy wiggle and a joyful flick of her tail, zoomed off to explore the lovely, safe perimeter of her new home. What a splendid day for measuring and for zoom-tastic adventures!
characters: Oren the kite maker, Plum the rabbit, Gran Maple
